comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. One polygon, way/682228180 (Stratton Mountain Resort, landuse=winter_sports with leisure=resort): the front face, Kidderbrook, the Snow Bowl, the Sun Bowl and the base village on one ticket and one map; it holds every lift and run whole. OSM has a second polygon of the same name (way/1367311040, landuse=winter_sports alone) over the same ground that also takes in the Sun Bowl lots, the Stratton Nordic Center and the condominiums east of it; the two overlap, so only one can be listed, and the tighter one is (both hold the same 183 lifts and runs whole). No other ski area lies in the box or the Overpass window. Every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-12 against Stratton's winter trail map (the James Niehues painting, 23-24-trailmap.pdf, made 2023-11-10, the map its trail-map page links; the Internet Archive's copy of 2026-01-07, the resort's site serving a bot wall): Illustrator vector labels over the painting, read at 200 to 400 dpi. Its trails are dashed lines in their rating's colour, with Easiest (green circle), More Difficult (blue square), Most Difficult (one black diamond), Experts Only (two) and an orange pill for a terrain park; glades are hatched green. The resort's lift and trail status loads in an interactive map behind the same bot wall, so the printed map is the only source and wins. Every trail the map names is in OSM (OSM names 116 runs, the connectors and the parks' own ways among them; the resort counts 99 trails), with the map's rating but four: Diamond in the Rough and the Dancing Bear line (expert in OSM, one diamond on the map) become advanced, Shortcut Big Ben (easy, a blue square) intermediate, and Daniel's Web's unrated line easy, as the map and its outline say. Names from the map: four glade outlines or lines whose other way has the map's spelling (Why Not for Why Now, Free Fall Gully for Freefall Gully, Moon Dance for Moondance, Shred Wood Forest for Shredwood Forest) and the Tyro Tube carpet (OSM Tryo Tube). Names that differ from the map only by a word or an abbreviation stay as OSM has them (Lower Liftline for LOWER LIFT LINE, Number 6 for NO. 6, Old Number 8 for OLD #8, Upper and Lower Grizzly Bear for GRIZZLY BEAR and LOWER GRIZZLY, Liftline Cut-thru, Buster's Trail, Upper and Lower Middlebrook for MIDDLE BROOK, Tyrolienne Park and East Byrnes Side Park for the parks, Summit Gondola for GONDOLA, Oso Carpet and Theodore Carpet for OSO and THEODORE). Parks: the five the map marks with an orange pill (Beeline, Betwixt, Tyrolienne, East Byrnes Side and Big Ben with its SBX course) get the park flag. Lifts: the map's 15 are in OSM (the Summit Gondola, Ursa Express, Snow Bowl Express, Shooting Star, Sunrise Express, American Express, Solstice, South American, Tamarack, Villager and the Cub Carpet, Oso, Theodore and Tyro Tube carpets, and the tube park's Slider); hidden: the Slider (tubing, as Vail's and Mt. Norquay's are) and the Catamount and Redlands carpets, which the map does not draw. OSM maps many of Stratton's runs twice, once on a service road carrying the run's piste tags and once as the run's own way (or as route-relation pieces on it): the 15 copies lying on another way of the same name for 94% to 100% of their length are hidden, so each run draws and ranks once; partial overlaps (Way Home, Overpass, Grizzly Access, Black Bear, Polar Bear, Big Ben, Solstice Way) stay. OSM gaps: none of the map's named runs is missing; the uphill routes the map draws in purple are not runs.
